news.story_lead: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement. Former Tamil Nadu finance minister and DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay's TVK government over its claim of lowering debt as he accused it of deliberately stalling development works. He alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement.

Former Tamil Nadu finance minister and DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay's TVK government over its claim of lowering debt as he accused it of deliberately stalling development works. He alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement. He made the remarks in response to reports that Tamil Nadu's borrowing through government bonds fell by 21% in the first half of the current fiscal year compared to the corresponding period last year. Thennarasu questioned the government, which came in power in April this year, over its silence on underlying economic realities. Also read: PM Modi attends Delhi Dussehra celebration, calls Ramlila the 'end of tyranny, terror' He said the TVK government is trying to present lower borrowing as a ‘massive achievement’. "But shouldn't they disclose how this debt requirement decreased? They must release full details of the capital expenditure and developmental works undertaken in this first half," Thennarasu said in a post on X. As he made contrast between with the previous DMK government's performance, Thennarasu highlighted allocation figures from the 2025–26 budget. "Under the DMK governance, ₹ 57,231 crore was allocated for capital expenditures. According to provisional monthly accounts of the CAG, ₹ 13,002.22 crore was spent effectively between April and September 2025 on key infrastructure projects, including the Metro Rail," he noted. Also read: Model Shraddha Dubey, sister and driver arrested in Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma's death case He raised several questions and demanded to know what the exact capital expenditure incurred by the TVK government was from April to September. "Can a government claim financial management accolades by delaying development works, withholding payments for completed projects, and artificially inflating cash reserves to borrow less," Thennarasu asked, adding, "Keeping pending dues unpaid cannot be classified as savings." Also, he pointed out a massive contradiction in the government's fiscal roadmap, revealing that while the TVK administration boasts of reduced borrowing in the first half, it has planned a massive borrowing spree of ₹ 48,000 crore for the October–December quarter alone. This figure is more than double the ₹ 23,500 crore raised in the preceding quarter. Also read: CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka move Delhi HC against 2-day extension of judicial custody While claiming that borrowings declined in the first half of the financial year, the TVK government has planned to borrow ₹ 48,000 crore in the October–December quarter alone. Is this not more than double the ₹ 23,500 crore borrowed in the previous quarter? He alleged that the decline in borrowings is because the TVK government is ‘struggling to undertake capital expenditure’ amid revenue collections that remain below the estimates projected in its budget. “Tenders worth tens of thousands of crores of rupees have been cancelled. Roads are in poor condition due to the lack of development works, construction projects remain incomplete, and thousands of people have lost their jobs,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. news.story_lead: Vijay govt faces BJP ire over parole to Coimbatore blast convicts: 'Justice can't be compromised for politics' Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead. The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to grant 60 days' parole to five life convicts of the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts case has received backlash from the BJP and triggered a row in the state. Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living.
news.full_article_text: Vijay govt faces BJP ire over parole to Coimbatore blast convicts: 'Justice can't be compromised for politics' Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead. The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to grant 60 days' parole to five life convicts of the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts case has received backlash from the BJP and triggered a row in the state. Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living. He added that the decision shows the government’s “one-sided lenient approach” towards convicted terrorists. In a post on X, Thirupathy said, “Granting long-term parole to those involved in the bombing incident that shattered many families is not only an insult to the memory of those who lost their lives but also a grave betrayal to the survivors.” “It sends the wrong message to the people of Tamil Nadu that those who wage war against society can also be shown mercy. Before the brutality of this terrorist attack, which is considered one of the darkest chapters in the state's history, personal reasons can never take precedence,” he added. Also Read: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims He added that BJP insists the revocation of the parole order immediately and hopes that no concessions are granted to convicts involved in this case. “The Bharatiya Janata Party insists that this 60-day parole order be revoked immediately and that no further concessions of any kind be granted to the 'Al-Umma' convicts involved in this case.” The BJP leader stressed that the terrorists must fully serve the sentences imposed on them as he said, “Justice for those affected by the Coimbatore bombing incident can never be compromised for political self-interest. Terrorists must fully serve the sentences imposed on them.” Also Read: Vijay’s TVK joins INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for the first time What happened in Coimbatore bomb blasts case As many as 58 persons were killed and 250 had suffered injuries when 19 bomb explosions rocked Coimbatore city in Tamil Nadu between February 14 and 17, 1998. The improvised explosive devices, with time delay mechanisms, had been placed in cars, two-wheelers, abandoned bags, push carts, tea cans and so on. SA Basha and Mohammed Ansari, leaders of Muslim militant organisation Al-Umma, were the prime convicts in the case. “Mohammed Ansari, Mohammed Ali, Monappa alias Mohammed Hasan, Mohammed Azam, and Nawab Khan were convicted as guilty. Planned and executed by the banned 'Al-Umma' terrorist organization ahead of an election campaign rally, this attack was a brutal massacre against innocent people. The Supreme Court itself described this act as "most heinous" and refused to grant bail to these convicts,” Thirupathy said on X. Of the 166 accused in the case, the trial court in August 2007 pronounced 69 persons guilty of different offences. In December 2009, the Madras high court upheld the convictions of 18 people – 17 life terms and one 13-year term – in the case. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. news.headline: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede
news.story_lead: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede The investigators are examining the CCTV footages to build the sequence of events that led to stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday. Over three days after 19 people were killed in Kolkata pandal stampede, the police are reportedly looking for a person who had allegedly misled revellers by announcing that a section of the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal was collapsing. The announcement reportedly triggered panic and led to the stampede on Saturday evening.
news.full_article_text: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede The investigators are examining the CCTV footages to build the sequence of events that led to stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday. Over three days after 19 people were killed in Kolkata pandal stampede, the police are reportedly looking for a person who had allegedly misled revellers by announcing that a section of the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal was collapsing. The announcement reportedly triggered panic and led to the stampede on Saturday evening. The police have not found evidence to substantiate the claim, news agency PTI quoted the police as saying. "At present, there is no evidence to suggest that any part of the pandal was in a position to collapse," the police officer said. The investigators are examining CCTV footage to establish the sequence of events, police said. Thirty cameras are installed across the premises, footage from 13 covers the area where the incident took place, according to the police. Deep Dive Police said the analysis indicates that rain caused the exit point to be congested, while the entry point remained open despite the presence of a large crowd inside the pandal. A stampede situation took place at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening, killing 19 and leaving 25 injured. The investigators are analysing the CCTV footage to reconstruct the crowd's movement and determine how the situation escalated, the officer said, adding that the circumstances under which entry was allowed despite congestion at the exit may also come under scrutiny. Police said that there are key questions as to who made the announcement and what was the purpose. The announcement that a section of the structure was collapsing allegedly triggered panic among visitors. "Police have not found evidence to substantiate the claim," the officer said. The mic announcement warning of a possible structural collapse is believed to be one of the reasons that led to crowd crush at the Kolkata pandal. According to the police, the announcement – “The condition of the pandal is very bad. It will collapse. Please leave” – was made inside the pandal as the crowd jostled through a narrow bylane on Saptami, the seventh day of the festival, while rain lashed the city and left the streets slippery. The announcement was also mentioned by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari as he said, "Preliminary investigation has revealed that it was an announcement by the organisers which led to the stampede-like situation and resulted in so many deaths.” Seven people – mostly the pandal organisers – have been arrested so far in connection with the stampede that occurred around 7.30pm at Chorbagan, one of the city’s most popular Durga Puja venues, in cramped north Kolkata. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. news.full_article_text: ‘Right to defend ourselves’: Jaishankar says India expects partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism S Jaishankar earlier held a meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is on a three-day visit to India. External affairs minister S Jaishankar said in Mumbai on Tuesday that India expects its partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism as he thanked the US administration under President Donald Trump for extraditing 26/11 attack mastermind Tahawwur Hussain Rana. Track live updates on day 1 of Rubio's India visit “We are clear on the right to defend ourselves against terrorism and expect our partners show zero tolerance towards terrorism,” Jaishankar said, making an indirect reference to US ties with Pakistan, which is accused of harbouring terrorists and plotting against India. Jaishankar made the remarks – during his address on American Independence Day celebration event in Mumbai – as he mentioned the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, often called 26/11 attacks, in which coordinated shooting and bombing attacks took place across the city over four days, from November 26 to 29. At least 175 people died in the attacks and over 300 were injured in one of the worst terror attacks in India. The attack was carried out by Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), a Pakistan-based terror outfit. Rubio's India visit Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit. Rubio and Jaishankar met earlier in the day where the leaders, along with UAE's foreign minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, where the leaders discussed regional energy security and way ahead on shared economic priorities. Jaishankar hosted Rubio for wide-ranging talks shortly after the top diplomat arrived in Mumbai for his second visit to India in under five months, even as bilateral ties remain strained over Washington's unpredictable trade policies and tightening immigration rules. Ahead of the meeting, the US Secretary of State described India as a crude oil refining "superpower" and advocated for processing more Venezuelan crude in India. The US Secretary of State is scheduled to visit Reliance Industries Ltd-owned Jamnagar Refinery on Wednesday. Rubio, answering a question on the proposed India-US trade pact, said "a small number of items" are left to be wrapped up and hoped that it will be sealed "shortly". "I would say we're about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly -- we're hoping, which it should -- and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter," he said. Following the meeting, Jaishankar said on social media that he and Rubio "shared views on further advancement of our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties." The US State Department said the secretary and the external affairs minister discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia. "The secretary reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India's supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand," it said. Jaishankar and Rubio, who travelled to India for the second time in less than five months with a large business delegation, met in the country’s financial hub against the backdrop of persisting strains in bilateral ties over a range of issues, including the Trump administration’s unpredictable trade policies, enhanced immigration restrictions affecting Indian professionals and the US’s growing proximity to Pakistan’s military leadership. EAM Jaishankar on meeting with Rubio Deep Dive After the meeting with Rubio, Jaishankar said on social media that they discussed ways to further advance “our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties”, and exchanged views on regional developments. Rubio said in a separate social media post that they “discussed energy security and defence cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the US-India strategic partnership”. Also Read | Rubio calls India ‘powerful, influential’, says India-US ties will define 21st century Purchases of American energy According to a readout from the US state department spokesman, Rubio pushed the Indian side to increase purchases of American energy, technologies and military and nuclear equipment. Rubio “reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India’s supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand," the readout said. Rubio commended progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and “advocated for the increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries”. There was no immediate response from Indian officials on Rubio’s comments. This was largely in line with the push from Washington during President Donald Trump’s second term for New Delhi to buy more energy, technology and military gear from the US. While India has diversified its energy sources over the past year, Russia remains the single largest source, accounting for more than 50% of all crude purchases, while the US was in third place with 5.1% in August. During a media interaction, Rubio described India as an important commercial and business partner of the US, a key member of the Quad and a strong strategic partner, and noted there is a “lot of defence cooperation” between the two sides. He also said the two sides are “very, very close” to finalising a bilateral trade deal. “I would say we’re about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly – we're hoping, which it should – and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter,” he said. A visit to the Reliance Industries-owned Jamnagar Refinery – currently the world’s largest with an installed capacity of 1.4 million barrels a day – is on Rubio’s itinerary for Wednesday, and he spoke extensively about the role of both India as a “refining superpower” and the Indian conglomerate in addressing global energy issues. Days before Rubio’s arrival in India, President Donald Trump waived sweeping new sanctions under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release hundreds of thousands of tonnes of Russian diesel onto the world market. Rubio noted that Indian companies can play a role in refining Venezuelan heavy crude as more of it enters the world market, an issue he planned to discuss during the visit to the Reliance refinery. “They have the capability to refine heavy crude, they have done so in the past. And I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do,” he said. “Refining capability is a key part of it and India is a refining superpower. They have the ability to do that and they have companies that know how to do that.” He also noted that Indian companies have pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela and can play a role in energy production. “With India, we've talked about it in the past…They're ready to do it, they're willing to do it. There might be a few impediments that stand in the way in terms of [pre-existing] sanctions,” he said. Asked about the reasons for his visit to the Reliance facility, Rubio replied: “Energy is related to national security. Countries fight wars over energy, economies collapse over lack of energy. We’re going to go see a company that has a tremendous amount of refining capability. It makes all the sense in the world to talk to them about it.” Rubio on India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy Rubio responded to another question about US satisfaction with India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy by noting that New Delhi has repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio and that the US can be an energy source. “Obviously, it’s not easy to do that from one day to the next. news.full_article_text: ‘Spend time with your families, remember Ashu, Saurav’: Abhijeet Dipke's emotional message to supporters ahead of festive season Abhijeet Dipke said that the consequences of the protests were also faced by their families of supporters and requested everyone to spend time with them. As Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka continue to be in jail, founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday made an emotional appeal to protestors and urged them to spend time with their families during the festive season. Dipke took to X as he thanked protestors for their support during past agitations and said that everyone had gone through a tough time during the protests. He added that the consequences were also faced by their families and requested everyone to spend time with them. “Hello cockroaches, how are you? I hope all of you are fine. I can see that for the past few days, all of you have been struggling really hard on the streets, in personal life, because of which we are putting up a fight. And I can understand what you are going through,” he said in a video message. Deep Dive Das and Ranka are lodged in Tihar Jail after they were arrested last week and sent to judicial custody for attempting to stage a protest at Jantar Mantar, which is now a de-notified protest cite. A Delhi magistrate court on Monday extended their judicial custody by two more days as it said the two CJP leaders ‘showed no respect for law’. "For a few days, spend time with your families. Be there with your families, be there with your loved ones," he said, adding, "Please remember Sourav and Ashu when you are with your families, because they both can't be with their families. So they are our family,” Dipke said in the social media post. Dipke rejects comparison to France, Bangladesh unrest The CJP leader also rejected comparisons between the outfit's protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the violent unrest in France, Nepal and Bangladesh. He said Das and Ranka "went to jail happily" and chose "peace over hatred" while following Mahatma Gandhi's path of satyagraha. “The people who have been doing this and that in France for the past few days, have some shame. Look at what is happening in India. In India, Sourav Das and Ashutosh went to jail with a smile,” he said. He said the CJP leaders had not resorted to violence despite being jailed and had accepted their imprisonment with a smile. “They did not do what was happening in France. When they knew they were being put in jail in a wrong way, yet they chose peace. They chose compassion and they went in jail with a smile, not with anger, not with hatred in their heart.” Dipke said the two had chosen peace and compassion despite believing they were being wrongfully imprisoned. He compared their approach to Gandhi's satyagraha, saying they were enduring imprisonment while upholding non-violence. “I think this is the biggest strength of our movement. And somewhere, I don't want to compare, this is not a comparison, but what Mahatma Gandhi did, when he was sent to jail, he went to jail quietly because he had a Satyagraha. And Ashutosh and Sourav are also doing the same Satyagraha.” The CJP and its supporters have been protesting against the SIR of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Das and Ranka were arrested after CJP activists entered Jantar Mantar on October 13, a day after it was removed from the list of designated protest sites. They were initially remanded to judicial custody for five days, with the custody extended by another two days on October 19. "I am telling you, when Sourav and Ashutosh will come out, they will again come out of jail with the same smile. news.headline: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family
news.story_lead: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead inside a medical shop on October 13. His family reused to cremate his body till a CBI inquiry was ordered. Seven days have passed since Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, was shot dead inside a medical store at a busy market in Mansa.
news.full_article_text: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead inside a medical shop on October 13. His family reused to cremate his body till a CBI inquiry was ordered. Seven days have passed since Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, was shot dead inside a medical store at a busy market in Mansa. However, he is yet to be cremated as his father, an ex-serviceman, Bhim Singh, had announced on October 13 that the family would not allow a post-mortem or conduct the last rites until the case is handed to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). But now Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has announced that the state government will hand over the probe into the murder case to the CBI. Jhota's murder on October 13 was livestreamed on Facebook. The Punjab government announcement came ahead of Union home minister Amit Shah's visit the family of Jhota and two other anti-drug activists killed in Punjab recently. Shah on Tuesday met the aggrieved families amid growing concerns over drug trafficking and law and order in Punjab. Deep Dive During his visit to Punjab, Shah went to the residence of late Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur to offer his condolences to the bereaved family. He also met with the family members of Gulzar Singh, who was killed for standing up against local chitta (synthetic drugs) peddlers in Sangrur. In a post shared on X, Shah expressed his grief, saying, "Today, at the residence of the family of late Bikramjit Singh ji, who lost his life for raising his voice against the unchecked drug trade in Punjab under the AAP government, I met them in Gurdaspur and expressed my condolences. May God grant them the strength to bear this sorrow." Amid Mann government's announcement of a CBI probe in Jhota's killing, Shah assured that the central agency will pursue the culprits involved in the killing regardless of their influence. “This morning, upon returning after celebrating his birthday, Bhagwant Mann Ji did one good thing—he handed over one inquiry to the CBI. I want to give my word to the people of Punjab: in the case handed over to us, whoever is found guilty—no matter how powerful or big they are—we will track them down even from the depths of the earth and hand them over to the law. We will bring them before the court,” Shah said in a dig at CM Mann, news agency PTI reported. "And today, I also want to appeal to the Chief Minister: you will not be able to handle it. Hand over the remaining two cases to the CBI as well. That is also the demand of their family members," he added. Shah said the ground reality described by the victims' families and residents was far more severe than what is captured in administrative files. "Meeting these three families, as well as the locals who were troubled and distressed by the chitta (drug) trade and had gathered at their homes—the reality of the situation in Punjab that they described turned out to be far more gut-wrenching and shattering than anything we read in official paper reports in Delhi," Shah said. Shah set a deadline of December 31, 2029, to eradicate the illicit narcotics network from Punjab, asserting that the Centre will track down and prosecute all perpetrators involved in the killings of anti-drug activists in the state. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. news.story_lead: Students gather at Delhi's Model Town park to burn 20-feet tall ‘Gyanesh Kumar effigy’, detained Police said the students were occupying space in a park, burning an effigy and protesting after which they were briefly detained. Several students and activists associated with Krantikari Yuva Sangathan were detained by the police on Tuesday after they burned the effigy of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar during Dussehra celebrations near Delhi’s Model Town. Krantikari Yuva Sangathan is a Delhi-based independent student and youth organisation.
news.full_article_text: Students gather at Delhi's Model Town park to burn 20-feet tall ‘Gyanesh Kumar effigy’, detained Police said the students were occupying space in a park, burning an effigy and protesting after which they were briefly detained. Several students and activists associated with Krantikari Yuva Sangathan were detained by the police on Tuesday after they burned the effigy of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar during Dussehra celebrations near Delhi’s Model Town. Krantikari Yuva Sangathan is a Delhi-based independent student and youth organisation. The alleged effigy-burning took place at Sangam Park near Model Town in northwest Delhi where the KYS students erected a 20-feet tall effigy with a poster of Gyanesh Kumar and slogans such as “Sack Gyanesh Kumar”, “Loot-tantra” and “Discrimination, Injustice”. The student organisation had made the announcement about burning the effigy of Kumar alongside Ravana on Monday. On Tuesday, the group was joined by some locals to burn the effigy but were stopped by the police. Jyoti, a Delhi University student associated with KYS, told HT, “We are well within our rights to burn a Ravana effigy. Why are they trying to protect Gyanesh from everything? We just want to show our dissent. The police came in. We don’t know who called them or if they were tracking us. There was a tussle but we still managed to burn the effigy. After burning the effigy, the policemen got angry and pushed us. Many of the students managed to leave but some were detained” Mudiya, the national spokesperson of KYS said the programme was organised to highlight the issue of irregularities in SIR of electoral polls. “Several activists were illegally detained by the police after the programme. Effigy burning is a form of freedom of speech and expression that is a fundamental right. Numerous judgments by high courts and the Supreme Court have upheld effigy burning as a form of expression protected under Article 19 of the Constitution of India.” A senior police officer said the protesters had not taken any permission for the protest and were burning effigy near a residential colony. “We had only removed a few protesters and detained 10-12 people. They were released within a few hours” said an officer. news.full_article_text: Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) - Published 19 October 2026 More than 70 security personnel were killed in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa on Monday, local authorities say. The Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response". The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations". Yemen's devastating civil war has flared up in recent months. At the start of October, pro-government forces launched a major offensive that aims to retake territory in western Yemen that is controlled by the Houthis. With air support from a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states, they managed to regain control of territory on the Red Sea coast that overlooks the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, which the Houthis captured in a surprise assault in September. However, fierce fighting is continuing there, as well as around the besieged government-controlled city of Taiz, and to the north in Marib and al-Jawf provinces. The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia. - Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says Published 4 days ago - On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged Published 12 October - 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Published 6 October Monday's attack in Shabwa was the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation. Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground at the camp. Hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and were forced to transfer the most seriously wounded people to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based, Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency. Shabwa's media office initially reported that 53 people were killed and 200 injured in the attack. But on Tuesday, it said in a new statement that Governor Awad bin al-Wazir had been informed by an investigative committee that the death toll was now 73, with another 14 individuals reported missing. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target. He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes". The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children. According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks. The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August. In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. Related topics
